data.long_meaning: Kishan is a Sanskrit name derived from the Sanskrit word 'kishor', meaning 'god in the form of a young boy'. The name signifies the grace and protection of a deity, and is often used for boys in Hindu tradition. The name Kishan carries the meaning “God's grace, deity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kishan usually hope their child will grow to embody god's grace, deity and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kishan has a significant cultural impact as it is deeply rooted in Hindu tradition. It is given to boys as a mark of blessings and protection from the divine. In Hindu mythology, Lord Krishna is popularly known as Kishan, and the name holds a special significance as it evokes the charming, young, and playful nature of the god.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Kishan holds immense spiritual significance as it signifies the presence and grace of a deity. It is believed that while the name Kishan is called upon, the deity is present and all worries are alleviated. The name invokes feelings of peace, protection, and happiness, and is a constant reminder of the divine presence in one's life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kishan: God as the embodiment of abundance and joy. The name Kishan is derived from Sanskrit 'Kishora', meaning young, youthful, or childlike, symbolizing the endless joy and enthusiasm of youth. It is also associated with Krishna, the divine god of love, compassion, and merriment, who bestows his blessings of prosperity and happiness upon his devotees.

vedic_reference.note: The name Kishan is derived from the Sanskrit word 'किशन्' (kishan), which is composed of the words 'किश्' (kish) meaning 'to give', and 'अन्' (an) meaning 'to or the one'. In Hindu mythology, Kishan is an avatar of the god Vishnu, who is known as the preserver of the universe. Kishan is often depicted as a young, playful, and mischievous deity who delights in granting boons and fulfilling the desires of his devotees.

historical_references.reference: According to the Hindu epic 'Ramayana', Kishan was the name of Lord Rama during his period of exile in the forest. This was the time when Lord Rama, along with his wife Sita and brother Lakshmana, lived in the forest as hermits.

Kishan was also a historical king of the Rajputs, ruling the kingdom of Mewar from 1424 to 1468 AD. He was a brave and just ruler who expanded the kingdom's territory and maintained peace within his realm.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Kishan continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
